newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel delays vote on Pena nomination.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel delays vote on Pena nomination.

text.p: The Senate Energy Committee has postponed a vote on the nomination of Federico Pena to be U.S. Secretary of Energy, the committee said on Tuesday.
It also canceled a vote on Tuesday on a bill that would require the Clinton administration to build a temporary storage facility for spent fuel from commercial nuclear reactors.
The two votes had been scheduled for Wednesday, but will now "likely be considered on Feb. 26," the committee said.
A Senate source said new questions had been raised concerning Pena, and would have to be answered before a vote on his nomination could go ahead.

The questions on Pena stemmed from a report in the Washington Times on Tuesday that said as Secretary of Transportation in 1994, Pena ordered Coast Guard contractors to rehire a minority business after it was terminated for poor performance.
Questions about the contract were raised in Pena's confirmation process.
The Washington Times quoted Pena denying having had anything to do with the rehiring of the company, DME Corp.

The vote on the nuclear waste bill, which utilities have pressed Congress to pass for the last two years, was postponed following a meeting on Tuesday between Senate leaders, President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.

Republicans on the energy committee had the votes to pass the bill, which the administration threatened to veto, and planned to negotiate changes with the White House before the bill came up for a vote on the Senate floor, a Senate source said.
"They said they do not want interim storage at all," the source said, citing comments by Gore at the meeting.

Instead of trying to negotiate with the administration, the Republicans plan now to try to build a bipartisan coalition in the Senate in a bid to override the threatened White House veto, the source said.
Energy Department officials were not immediately available to comment on the delay.
